title: I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire
summary: Harlan Leonard's too-fast version failed, while Tommy Tucker's number-one hit of Durham's song with Benny Benjamin used the right tempo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And Harlan Leonard did I Don't Want To Set The World On Fire, but he did it up in a speed tempo and that's why he didn't get over with that particular song. The same song would have caught right with the public. But when Tommy Tucker --
Was that -- whose song was that?
Myself and Benny Benjamin, we was writing together at that time.
Oh, that's right, yeah. Well, that must have been one of your biggest.
Yeah, it is one of the biggest, yeah.
Who made the hit on that?
Tommy Tucker got number one hit on it, just on the records. Then others followed up.
